title: Why the ranker comes after retrieval
summary: What a two-tower model can and cannot do.

choices.text: Item embeddings can be computed offline for the whole catalogue because the item tower does not depend on the user.
A two-tower model can use "how many times has this user watched this creator" as an input.
Training with in-batch negatives over-penalises popular items unless you correct for how often each item is sampled.
An ANN index trades a little recall for search over millions of vectors in milliseconds.
Two-tower retrieval removes the need for a separate ranker, because its dot product is already the best score.
